title: Homelessness payments to nonprofits per household moved into housing
question: How much did the homelessness department pay nonprofits for each household it moved into supportive housing or rapid rehousing?
finding: Per household moved into supportive housing or rapid rehousing: $129,153 in 2019 and $212,345 in 2026 (+64%), as the money went from $158.9 million to $518.3 million (+226%) and the count from 1,230 to 2,441 (+98%).
how: Money as in the previous screen. Count: households that moved into permanent supportive housing plus households housed through rapid rehousing, added up from the twelve monthly figures on the City scorecard for each fiscal year (July to June). The monthly figures are not de-duplicated across the year.
limits: The count is the homelessness department's own, published by the Controller; no outside body counts move-ins. Move-ins depend on how many homes open or turn over in a year, which jumped when hotels were bought in 2021 and 2022. The money is everything the department paid nonprofits that year, so this is the cost of the whole system set against one result, not the price of that result: most of the money keeps people housed, sheltered or in care who are not counted as a new result. A falling count can reflect harder cases or fewer openings rather than weaker work, and the pandemic distorted 2020 to 2022.
